marks.gloss_en: למדתי שמתפללין בדרך -- learned from Eliyahu's 'you should have prayed on the road'
למדתי שהמתפלל בדרך מתפלל תפלה קצרה -- learned from Eliyahu's 'you should have prayed a short prayer'
lesson 1: one does not enter a ruin
Eliyahu: you should have prayed on the road [rather than enter the ruin]
R' Yose heard a bat kol cooing like a dove and saying: woe, that I destroyed my house, burned my sanctuary and exiled my children among the nations of the world
the baraita: one does not enter a ruin -- for three reasons
דתניא, רבי אליעזר אומר: שלש משמרות הוי הלילה -- the baraita corroborates that R' Eliezer holds three watches
the night consists of three watches
the night consists of four watches (proposed as what R' Eliezer might hold)
the signs: first watch -- a donkey brays; second -- dogs howl; third -- an infant nurses and a wife converses with her husband
he counts the starts of the watches (rejected: the first watch's start needs no sign -- it is simply evening)
he counts the end of the first watch, the start of the last, and the middle of the middle
the use of the last watch's sign: one sleeping in a dark house rises and recites the Shema when the wife converses and the infant nurses
